By accepting optional cookies, you consent to allowing us and our partners to store and access personal data on your device, such as browsing behaviour and unique identifiers. You can find further information, and change your preferences via 'Manage preferences'.

This cholesterol drug promised to be a game-changer. Why did it flop in the clinic — and is there still hope?

Physicians were excited about several therapies that slash levels of lipoprotein(a) — an important cardiovascular risk factor.

Featured Content
Chinese doctoral students in clinical medicine can graduate without a thesis — more degrees to follow

Postgraduate students studying professional medicine degrees can qualify with a ‘practical achievement’.

Xiaoying You

‘A perfect scientist, a perfect mum’: researchers mourn two biologists’ deaths in Spanish train crash

Scientists pay tribute to Marta Shahbazi Alonso and Tamara González Costa who died on their way to a developmental-biology meeting.

Miryam Naddaf
News02 Nov 2026
Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert

A geoarchaeological survey of the Rub’ al Khali (the Empty Quarter of Arabia) and spatial modelling of the Arabian Peninsula suggest that human settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and stone suitable for making tools, rather than water alone.

Rudolf W. DellmourEmily CocoJeffrey I. Rose

Explore how researchers debunked race science. Plus, pressure put on your bones by exercise might slow ageing and watch a snake do a forward roll to escape danger.

Flora Graham

Accounting of Africa’s water reveals a management gap

A map of Africa’s water demand reveals that the scarcity of water is only part of the problem facing the continent — management is a separate challenge.

Xu Wang

Tethered to stone: how rock and water availability shaped early desert occupation

Fresh water in deserts often points to sites with signs of early humans and stone tools. But, in Arabia’s Rub’ al Khali region, water alone does not predict occupation.

Emanuele Cancellieri
News & Views28 Oct 2026
Lactate takes a shortcut into mitochondria to power the heart

A cellular fuel called lactate is channelled directly into energy-generating organelles in heart muscle, defying the prevailing view about lactate transport.

Trace ThomeZolt Arany
News & Views28 Oct 2026
Clues about complex life come from freshly cultivated archaea

Two archaeal strains that belong to a lineage closely related to the ancestor of eukaryotic cells (complex cells with membrane-bound organelles) have been brought into culture. Their simple internal organization, elaborate surface structures, microbial partnerships and protein-dependent lifestyle provide clues about how eukaryotic cells arose.
